reasoning: The claim's own hypotheses state that f satisfies a linear recurrence of order at most 2, and the observable is f(n) mod 2711. 2711 is prime (trial division to 52, asserted in fit_recurrence.py), so the observations live in the field GF(2711) and an order-<=2 homogeneous recurrence there is fixed by four consecutive values. I sampled f(1..6) mod 2711 = 20, 116, 740, 2253, 1568, 899 and solved the 2x2 system on (f1..f4) over GF(2711) (determinant nonzero, inverted by Fermat), giving f(n) = 10*f(n-1) + 2690*f(n-2) = 10*f(n-1) - 21*f(n-2) mod 2711. The two samples not used in the fit, n=5 and n=6, are predicted exactly, which is the first independent check. The characteristic polynomial x^2-10x+21 factors as (x-3)(x-7) and the closed form is f(n) = 2*(3^n + 7^n) mod 2711; closed_form.py confirms it agrees with the recurrence on n=1..1200. All arithmetic is exact integer arithmetic modulo a prime -- no floating point is used, so there is no precision question. With the recurrence in hand the whole domain is computable locally at zero metered cost: f(n) mod 2711 = 1822 for NO n in [1, 600]. This is an exhaustive check of the full stated domain (600 points), not a bounded search inside a larger domain. Stronger still, since ord(3)=1355 and ord(7)=2710 the sequence is periodic with period dividing 2710, and an exhaustive scan of a full period n=1..2710 finds no n at all with f(n) mod 2711 = 1822, so the proposition holds not just on [1,600] but for every n >= 1. I then spent three metered calls specifically to falsify the reconstructed model rather than to confirm it: sample(600) at the far end of the domain returned 2111 (predicted 2111), and sample(474) -- the closest approach in the domain, where the model says f = 1820, only 2 away from the forbidden residue and hence the point where a wrong model is most likely to flip the verdict -- returned 1820 (predicted 1820). evaluate(474) returned holds=true, confirming the verdict interface agrees with the value interface at that point. Model and metered oracle agree at every point queried, including both extremes of risk. The residual risk is that f departs from an order-<=2 recurrence somewhere in [1,600] that I did not probe; that would contradict a stated hypothesis of the claim, and it is further constrained by the exact agreement at n=600 and at the single nearest-miss point.
route_taken: Rather than testing points, I bought the generator: 6 samples to identify the order-<=2 recurrence over GF(2711) (4 to solve, 2 as held-out prediction checks), which turns the remaining 594 points into free local computation, then spent 3 more metered calls to attack the reconstructed model at its weakest points (n=600, the domain edge, and n=474, the closest approach to the forbidden residue) instead of buying a range(1,600) scan that would have cost 600 and told me nothing about why.
